Duration construction¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

pluss::Duration pluss::duration::nanos(std::int64_t count);
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::nanos(std::initializer_list<NestedInt64Literal> nested);
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::nanos(pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t> flat, pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t> sizes);
// microseconds/milliseconds/seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks each have the same three overloads as nanos above.

pluss::Duration pluss::duration::microseconds()
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::milliseconds();
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::seconds();
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::minutes();
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::hours();
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::days();
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::weeks()

enum class pluss::duration::Unit { Nanos, Microseconds, Milliseconds, Seconds, Minutes, Hours, Days, Weeks };
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::make(std::int64_t count, Unit unit);
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::make(std::initializer_list<NestedInt64Literal> nested, Unit unit);
pluss::Duration pluss::duration::make(pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t> flat, pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t> sizes, Unit unit);

pluss::Duration pluss::duration::range(const Duration& start, const Duration& end, const Duration& step);

What It Does¶

Builds a Duration — an elapsed-time value or array — from scratch, with no Timeline required.

Duration (capital D, the type) has no public constructors and no public construction statics of its own — Duration() is deleted, and there is no Duration::from_scalar_nanos/Duration::range to call directly. Construction lives entirely in its own namespace, pluss::duration (lowercase), the same split as pluss::timeline::make/pluss::timeline::from_epoch being kept separate from Timeline itself:

  • pluss::duration::nanos(...): the base unit. microseconds/milliseconds/ seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks all scale up from it, so every unit factory produces an indistinguishable Duration for an equal elapsed time — days(1) and hours(24) are the same value.

  • Every one of those eight functions has three overloads, not just a scalar one — see Example 2. A single count builds a scalar (0D) Duration; a braced list builds 1D; a nested braced list (up to 3D) or an explicit (flat, shape) pair builds any N-D array — mirroring pluss::timeline::make’s own scalar/1D/nested/flat+shape overload set exactly. Plain {...} braces work directly for the flat/shape arguments too (see Example 3) — no explicit RangeView wrapping needed.

  • pluss::duration::make(values, unit): the same three-overload shape again, generalized to take the unit as a runtime Unit value instead of picking a function by name — for call sites where the unit isn’t known until runtime (read from config, chosen generically). See Example 4.

  • pluss::duration::range(start, end, step): a pandas-timedelta_range-style constructor that always builds a 1D array, regardless of how start/end/ step themselves were built.

Parameters¶

count (std::int64_t)

A single count in the named unit, for the scalar overload. Negative values are valid and represent “backward in time” — see abs.

nested (nested std::initializer_list<std::int64_t>, up to 3 levels deep)

A braced literal — {1, 2, 3} for 1D, {{1, 2}, {3, 4}} for 2D, and so on — of counts in the named unit.

flat, sizes (pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t>)

An explicit flat buffer of counts plus the target shape, for constructing any rank without going through nested braces — the same explicit-shape escape hatch pluss::timeline::from_epoch(flat, sizes) offers for Timeline. Accepts a plain {...} brace list directly; pluss::RangeView<T> converts implicitly from std::initializer_list<T>.

unit (pluss::duration::Unit, make only)

Which unit count/nested/flat are expressed in.

start, end, step (const Duration&, range only)

Inclusive start, exclusive-past-end stop, and step size, exactly like pluss::timeline::date_range for Timeline or Python’s range(). All three are themselves Duration values (typically scalar, built from one of the unit factories above), not raw integers.

Returns¶

Duration A scalar (0D), 1D, or N-D Duration depending on which overload is used. range always returns 1D.

Examples¶

Example 1. The friendly scalar unit factories, including a negative count.

auto ninety_min = pluss::duration::minutes(90);
auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
auto one_day = pluss::duration::days(1);
auto neg_fifteen_min = pluss::duration::minutes(-15);
std::cout << pluss::duration::print(ninety_min);

Output¶

Duration(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1)
0 days 01:30:00.000000000

pluss::duration::print (or std::cout << ninety_min directly, since Duration has an operator<<) is the natural way to read a Duration back — no unit conversion needed. ninety_min.total().nanoseconds(), which would give the same value as a plain number (5.4e12 nanoseconds), is the total().nanoseconds() family’s job instead, useful when you need a numeric Series rather than a human-readable rendering.

Example 2. N-D construction: a 1D list and a nested 2D literal, for minutes/hours respectively.

auto minutes_1d = pluss::duration::minutes({15, 30, 45, 60});
auto hours_2d = pluss::duration::hours({{1, 2}, {3, 4}, {5, 6}});
std::cout << "1d.dim=" << minutes_1d.dim() << " 1d.numel=" << minutes_1d.numel() << "\n";
std::cout << "2d.dim=" << hours_2d.dim() << " 2d.numel=" << hours_2d.numel() << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::series::print(hours_2d.total().hours());

Output¶

1d.dim=1 1d.numel=4
2d.dim=2 2d.numel=6
Series(shape=[3,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1.0000 2.0000 ⎤
⎢ 3.0000 4.0000 ⎥
⎣ 5.0000 6.0000 ⎦

hours_2d is a genuine 2D Duration with shape [3, 2], holding 1 through 6 hours in row-major order — not six independent scalar Durations.

Example 3. Explicit (flat, shape) construction with plain braces — no RangeView wrapping needed, it converts implicitly.

auto days_2x2 = pluss::duration::days({1, 2, 3, 4}, {2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(days_2x2.total().days());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1.0000 2.0000 ⎤
⎣ 3.0000 4.0000 ⎦

Example 4. pluss::duration::make — the same construction, with the unit picked at runtime.

auto made_scalar = pluss::duration::make(3, pluss::duration::Unit::Days);
auto made_1d = pluss::duration::make({1, 2, 3}, pluss::duration::Unit::Hours);
std::cout << "scalar=" << pluss::series::print(made_scalar.total().days()) << "\n";
std::cout << "1d=" << pluss::series::print(made_1d.total().hours());

Output¶

scalar=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=3.0000
1d=Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.0000, 2.0000, 3.0000]

Example 5. pluss::duration::range builds a real 1D array with no Timeline involved.

auto steps = pluss::duration::range(
    pluss::duration::days(0), pluss::duration::days(10), pluss::duration::days(2));
std::cout << "dim=" << steps.dim() << " numel=" << steps.numel() << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::duration::print(steps);

Output¶

dim=1 numel=6
Duration(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6)
[ 0 days 00:00:00.000000000, 2 days 00:00:00.000000000, 4 days 00:00:00.000000000, 6 days 00:00:00.000000000, 8 days 00:00:00.000000000, 10 days 00:00:00.000000000 ]

Six values from 0 up to (but not including) 10, stepping by 2 — the same half-open range convention as pluss::timeline::date_range.

Notes¶

  • Duration() has no default constructor, and there is no public Duration::from_scalar_nanos/Duration::range either — always go through pluss::duration::*.

  • The unit factories are pure convenience: nothing they produce is distinguishable afterward from an equivalent duration::nanos call at the same elapsed magnitude — Duration has no internal notion of “the unit it was constructed in.”

  • Every unit factory’s N-D overloads (Examples 2 and 3) exist precisely so you never have to fall back to building an array of scalar Durations by hand and combining them — construct the array directly, in one call. make (Example 4) gets the same N-D overload set, for when the unit itself is a runtime value.

  • Timeline - Timeline is an implicit way to obtain a Duration outside this factory entirely — see Timeline::diff.

See Also¶

  • add, sub, mul, div: combining and scaling Duration values once constructed.

  • total().seconds(): converting a Duration back into a plain Series in a chosen unit.

  • Timeline::diff: the Timeline-side source of a Duration.
